fields.beat: The player character's intro, for the Founding peoples.

script.note: Dawn. The player walks the Coast Road through the ash fields toward Ashford; the refinery stacks glow ahead.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: The Coast Road ends where the ash fields begin, and the ash fields end at {ashford}.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: You have a profession, a pack, and coin for a week. You do not have a class, a ship, or a plan past the harbour.

script.note: A carter passes and nods; nobody looks twice. Founding peoples pass unremarked.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Nobody looks twice at you. In {ashford} that is a kind of luck.

script.note: A pinned notice at the city gate: "Crews wanted. Ask at {sallows_exchange}."

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Every notice on the gate says the same thing: ask at {sallows_exchange}.

fields.beat: The player character's intro, for the Beastkin.

script.note: Dawn on the Coast Road. A gate clerk checks papers.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Every beastkin family can name its home rock. Yours is two days' sail behind you, and {ashford} is in front.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: The gate clerk asks for your island before your name, and writes the island down first.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: You have a profession, a pack, and coin for a week. You do not have a class, or a ship.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: The clerk points without looking up. Work, ships and crews: {sallows_exchange}, by the port.

fields.beat: The player character's intro, for the Fae.

script.note: Dawn on the Coast Road. The refinery's haze makes the player's outline shimmer; a child points.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Fae are closer to unfixed than anyone alive, and {ashford} burns the unfixed sea for fuel. The stacks are lit all night.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: A child on a cart points at you, and her mother pulls her arm down. Not cruelly. Just quickly.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: You have a profession, a pack, and coin for a week. No class, no ship.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: The notices at the gate all point one way: {sallows_exchange}, by the port.

fields.beat: The player character's intro, for the Monsterkin.

script.note: Dawn at the city gate. A guard steps out with a ledger.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: "Monster" is what the Compact writes on the manifest. The gate guard writes it on yours.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Surety, he says: a bond before you can stay inside the walls overnight. You don't have it. You have a profession, a pack, and coin for a week.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: He lets you through for the day. The quay inns won't take you, he adds, except one.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Work, ships and crews are at {sallows_exchange}. He says it like he expects you'll be back at the gate by dusk.

data.name: A hard time at the Exchange

script.note: Inside {sallows_exchange}. {protag2} and {protag3} are already at the high desk; the player joins the queue behind them.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: A crow with a satchel full of somebody else's pens. No.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: They're my pens. Now.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: And a Trollblood who wants a berth on a ship. Dear heart, I can't even get you a bed.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: I sleep on deck. I'm first up and last down. Write that on whatever you write.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: And you, {pc}. Let me guess. Big plans, no class.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Everyone is. Sit down, the three of you, and stop blocking my door.

script.note: The door bangs. {enkrid} comes in out of breath, a pocket watch chain swinging.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: {ashford}. Is this where the legends' crews hire? {captain}'s people?

script.speaker: broker
script.text: {captain} has been gone eight years, little road fae. And now there are four of you.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Here is the part none of you will like. No captain in this harbour signs on unclassed crew. Not even for the galley. Get bound, then come back.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: How much is binding?

script.speaker: broker
script.text: More than you have. All four together, more than you have.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Then we put it together.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: Together. Yes.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: You've known each other a minute and a half.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Then it's a good minute and a half. Give us work. And answer questions.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Oh, I'll answer your stupid, basic, and naive questions. Questions are free today. Tomorrow they're a silver each.

script.note: Opens the broker's question menu (see the Questions entry). Then the commission.

fields.beat: Deck event 02, beat 4: the broker answers their questions. The game's tutorial menu; each Heading 2 is one question.

Q: What is a class?: What binding gives you. Brume possibility bound into your body, and with it the way you fight. Until you're bound you can swing a stick like anyone; after, you're a Vanguard, a Theorist, whatever you pay for.
Q: What is a profession?: What you do when nobody's trying to kill you. Anyone can learn one. It's how you earn, mend, chart and cook, and in a harbour it matters more than your class.
Q: What is grade?: How firmly a thing is written into the world. You're F, or you will be once you're bound. Water has a grade too. Sail into water above your grade and it will tell you so.
Q: Why won't ships take unclassed crew?: Because the sea outside the Reach is unfixed, and unfixed water eats the unbound. Insurers won't cover you. Captains won't carry what the insurers won't.
Q: Who runs Ashford?: The Compact owns the refinery, the licences and most of the captains. The Bench owns the charts. I own what everyone tells me.
Q: Where did the legends' crew go?: Out past Kelder's Wall, eight years ago, on the best-found ship that ever left this quay. Nobody's heard a word. That's the honest answer. The dishonest ones cost more.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Work, then. One job pays enough to bind four. {merchant}, charge-lamp money on {refinery_row}. His daughter {petra} went into the {undercourses} four days ago and hasn't come out.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Into the sewers. On purpose.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: She saw something from her window and went to look. Rich girls do.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: Something's off. Why hasn't anyone taken it?

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Someone did.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: And?

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Three Coldwater sellswords, six days ago. They haven't come out either.

script.note: Beat. Everyone looks at each other.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Then the pay goes up.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: The pay is the pay.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Then you lend us gear. We have a pack each and a stolen pen.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Loaners. Basic blades, a lamp, a pry bar. Bring them back whole or pay for them.

script.note: The heroes receive the loaned gear: one basic weapon each, a charge lamp, a pry bar. Marked "Loaned".
Outside, on the Exchange steps, the four check their gear. Bonding beat.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Four people, one job, zero classes. I've had worse crews.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: You've had a crew?

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: I've had a dock. Same thing with fewer oars.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: {captain}'s crew started in this harbour too. Did you know that?

script.note: {enkrid} takes out the pocket watch. The flashback begins: the Prologue entry.

fields.beat: Deck event 01, all seven beats, told as {enkrid}'s flashback when he first opens up to the group.

script.note: Flashback filter. Night in {enkrid_village}. A small {enkrid}, maybe nine, curled on the ground behind a hovel.

script.speaker: dov
script.text: Road fae. Horns like a goat and legs like a stork. Get up so we can knock you down again.

script.note: The boys kick him. Nobody from the fire comes.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Nobody ever came. Nobody stood up for an orphaned road fae.

script.speaker: captain
script.text: That's enough. Go home, all of you, before I decide you're crew and put you to work.

script.note: The boys scatter. {captain} kneels. Behind her, {first_mate} with a chart case and {inventor} with a toolbag full of brass.

script.speaker: captain
script.text: Life is worth living, little one. If only to see what the world's still hiding.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: They were recruiting. Strong backs and quick hands, for an expedition past anything anyone had charted.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: I can work. I can fix things. I fixed the chapel clock.

script.speaker: first_mate
script.text: How old are you? Nine? The Sea of Possibility doesn't care how clever you are. Grow first. Learn first.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: They said no. He was bruised, and small, and nine.

script.speaker: inventor
script.text: Wait. We can't leave him here like this.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: So they paid. Four years at the Wright chapel: schooling, room and board, Brother Ansel's patience.

script.speaker: captain
script.text: When you're grown and done with school, come and find us. Ashford Roads. Any captain there will know our names.

script.speaker: inventor
script.text: Here. It keeps time, and it'll remind you what you're keeping time for.

script.note: {inventor} gives him the crystal-faced, engraved pocket watch. Close-up on the engraving (the user to write what it says).

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: They left the next morning on the expedition they'd planned, and were never heard from again.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Everyone said they were lost. {enkrid} wound the watch every night and decided everyone was wrong.

script.note: Flashback ends on the Exchange steps.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: They're alive. I'm going to find them.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Then we'd better get bound. Sewers first.

script.note: The heroes drop through a culvert hatch under Refinery Row. Warm, foul air. Rat noise everywhere.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: It's warm. Why is a sewer warm?

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: Refinery run-off. Forty years of it.

script.note: A side tunnel: three bodies in Coldwater colours, gnawed. A dropped journal.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: The sellswords. All three.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Rats did this. Look at the marks. Lots of rats.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: Rats don't usually finish a person.

script.note: The journal's last page: "Something in the big cistern. Lamps don't scare it. Light does." Kept as a clue item.
A rat the size of a pony, with a dozen smaller rats. Battle: {old_gnaw} and a rat swarm. Unclassed heroes: Strike, Aid, Stabilise, items.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: That is not a rat. That's a rat's landlord.

script.note: After the win, no casualties.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: We did that. Unclassed, with loaners.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: We did that. Keep going.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Confident now, they pressed on.

fields.beat: Deck event 03, beats 4-6. A fight they can't win: the battle ends after two rounds with the party pushed back, no one lost.

script.note: The Grate Chamber. {petra} is huddled on a ledge. Something made of dark and teeth uncoils in the cistern: {gloam}.

script.speaker: petra
script.text: Don't! It doesn't stop!

script.note: Battle: {gloam}. Its Resistance is far beyond the party. After two rounds it throws them back to the doorway.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Everything I hit, it just isn't there anymore.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Fighting it isn't working. Look at the room instead.

script.note: A shaft of daylight through the street grate falls in a bright square on the floor. {gloam} flows around it, every time.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: It won't touch the light.

script.speaker: petra
script.text: It goes still when the sun comes through. Every day, around noon. That's how I'm alive.

fields.beat: Deck event 03, beats 7-9. A Scene on the battle screen: get the Gloam into the light before the sun moves off. Resistance is the timing; Setbacks damage the loaned gear.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: So we put it in the light.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: The light's moving. The sun doesn't wait for us.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: Then we move faster than the sun.

script.note: Scene approaches, shown before the player picks: Bait it (Full, Combat Effort, takes hits). Block its exits (Full, Athletics). Angle the light with the charge lamp's mirror or by prying the grate wider (Full for Tinker, Half for others). Rig a line to drag the grate cover (Full for Sailor). Talk to Petra and read its pattern (Half, Craft Effort). Aid (Half).
Setbacks hit hit points and the loaned gear; each Setback marks one loaner Damaged.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: They had underestimated how long the sun would take. They took every hit while it crawled across the floor.

script.note: Win: {gloam} is caught in the light, goes rigid, and comes apart into warm grey fog that settles in the water. {petra} is free.

script.speaker: petra
script.text: You came all the way down here for me?

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: For your father's money. But also for you. Mostly the money.

script.note: Back at the Exchange. Petra is home; the fee is paid. The broker inspects the battered loaners.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Bent, chipped, cracked, and is that tooth marks? You'll pay for these.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Then they're ours.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Then they're yours. Which leaves you short of four bindings by a little.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: The sellswords' journal said light. You knew what was down there.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: I suspected.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Suspected is a word that costs a danger fee.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Unless you'd like Coldwater to hear how their sellswords died.

script.note: Beat. The broker counts out more coin.

script.speaker: broker
script.text: Danger fee. Don't come back for a week. Actually, come back. I like you. I'll deny it.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: Just enough to bind four. Not a copper over.

script.note: The loaned gear is now owned. The broker's commissions board opens: F-grade work around Ashford.

fields.beat: Deck event 04, beat A. The player picks a class here; the trio take theirs from the story.

script.note: The Binding House: a white hall, brass coils, glass cylinders of warm grey brume.

script.speaker: binder
script.text: Cash or Compact debt?

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Cash. All of it.

script.speaker: binder
script.text: Rare. Choose your binding.

script.note: The player chooses one of the twelve F-grade classes. The trio: {enkrid} Bloodcharged, {protag2} Theorist, {protag3} Vanguard.

script.speaker: binder
script.text: Hold still. I've stopped promising it won't hurt.

script.note: Binding: the brume flows in. White light. Everyone staggers. {enkrid} drops.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: Is he breathing? He's fae. Is it different for fae?

script.speaker: binder
script.text: Fae take in more than they should. He'll live. He'll want a bed.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Then he gets a bed. We stick together.

script.note: They carry {enkrid} to {lantern_lee}.

data.name: A night at the Lantern and Lee

fields.beat: Deck event 04, beat C. They stay the night. Optional talks with each of the trio (party bonding).

script.speaker: innkeeper
script.text: Monsterkin, fae, crow and whatever you are. One room. I don't ask, you don't break anything.

script.note: Optional: talk to each of the trio before sleeping.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: I've never been bound before. I can feel the floor through my boots. I can feel the whole quay.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: My father would call this a waste of a good family's money. It's the first thing I've ever bought myself.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: The watch stopped when I fell. It's ticking again now.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: They slept late. Much too late.

data.name: The Gilded Tern leaves without them

fields.beat: Deck events 04 to 05: delayed, they meet the nobles and miss the first ship. The demo ends here.

script.note: Midmorning. The heroes run onto the Long Quay. {gilded_tern} is loading. {rourke} stands at the gangway with {noble} and her retinue.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Captain! Four bound crew, ready to sign!

script.speaker: rourke
script.text: Four bound crew. Yesterday I'd have taken you. This morning, {noble} needs the berths for her household.

script.speaker: noble
script.text: Is that a troll?

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: Trollblood. And I'm crew.

script.speaker: rourke
script.text: Not on my ship. No offence to your blood. It's business.

script.note: The gangway comes up. {gilded_tern} slips its lines.

script.speaker: enkrid
script.text: That was our ship.

script.speaker: protag2
script.text: That was a ship.

script.speaker: protag3
script.text: There'll be another. There's always another ship.

script.speaker: narrator
script.text: The first ship left without them.

script.note: End of the demo. Title card: "Possibilities". The next chapter begins with the Second Captain.
